connectors.refdes: Form 2 mains power input · external connection
connectors.form: Power-entry connector face and contact count not specified by reviewed official source
connectors.scope: Formlabs technical specifications give 100–240 V AC, 1.5 A, 50/60 Hz and 65 W. The official Form 2 glossary says the internal PSU converts line power to +24 V DC. Connector type, individual input contacts, protective-earth terminal and installed power-cord details are not established here. No SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: USB connector subtype and contact count unknown from reviewed Form 2 source
connectors.scope: Formlabs identifies a rear USB port and says the supplied cable connects it to a computer. The source does not identify the Form 2 connector subtype or pin schedule. Do not infer USB-C from later Form 4 models. No SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: RJ-45/8P8C interface; eight connector reference positions
connectors.scope: Formlabs identifies a rear RJ-45 Ethernet LAN port and 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX connectivity. Contacts 1–8 below are connector-reference positions only; the reviewed Form 2 documentation does not assign per-contact LAN functions or establish a Formlabs mating-view drawing. No SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: Wireless interface; no external machine contact schedule
connectors.scope: Formlabs states Form 2 has built-in Wi-Fi configured from the touchscreen. No external antenna connector or machine contact schedule is established by the reviewed Form 2 sources. Reference context only; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.refdes: Front touchscreen to motherboard ribbon connection
connectors.form: Ribbon cable connection; pin count and pinout unknown
connectors.scope: The Formlabs Form 2 glossary identifies a motherboard connector linked to the front display by a ribbon cable, but gives no contact count or pin schedule. Internal interface only; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: Motor connector and winding-contact schedule unknown
connectors.scope: Formlabs identifies one of three motherboard-driven stepper motors as the build-platform motor. Its connector positions and coil map are not provided by the reviewed source. Internal machine context; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: Motor connector and winding-contact schedule unknown
connectors.scope: Formlabs identifies one of three motherboard-driven stepper motors as the wiper motor. Its connector positions and coil map are not provided by the reviewed source. Internal machine context; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.refdes: Tank-carrier stepper motor · internal motor connection
connectors.form: Motor connector and winding-contact schedule unknown
connectors.scope: Formlabs identifies one of three motherboard-driven stepper motors as the tank-carrier motor. Its connector positions and coil map are not provided by the reviewed source. Internal machine context; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: Integrated motor drivers; no external driver-input contacts documented
connectors.scope: Formlabs says three motor-driver chips on the motherboard control the build-platform, wiper and tank-carrier motors. These are inside the Form 2; the reviewed sources do not document an external step/direction/enable interface. Reference context only; no SmoothieBox route.

connectors.form: Internal optical subsystem; electrical connector schedule unknown
connectors.scope: Formlabs describes a 405 nm violet diode laser with maximum output 250 mW and Class 1 product classification. No external laser power supply or machine-side electrical contact schedule is identified. Reference context only; no SmoothieBox route.

evidence.primary: Formlabs Form 2 Product Glossary, Form 2 connection instructions, and Form 2 technical specifications
evidence.scope_note: Formlabs machine-side hardware remains electrically separate from SmoothieBox. Only externally identified RJ-45 contact positions are counted and enumerated; USB and power connector positions, the display ribbon, motor connectors, driver interfaces, Wi-Fi antenna interface and laser contacts remain unknown. No dotted guesses, solid routes or DB25 peripheral are established.
